items.title: Bengaluru: Traffic curbs on Ballari Road for 18 months as BDA begins corridor work
items.summary: Commuters travelling on Ballari Road will face traffic restrictions for the next 18 months as the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) begins construction of an elevated corridor on Friday, November 6. The restrictions will affect commuters travelling between Hebbal, central Bengaluru and Kempegowda International Airport (KIA). The Bengaluru Traffic Police have prohibited all goods vehicles, including light, medium and heavy goods vehicles, as well as KSRTC and private buses, from using the affected stretch. Cars, two-wheelers and school buses can continue to use the road. The four-lane elevated corridor will run between the University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS) staff quarters and Mehkri Circle, covering around 1.6 km. The stretch falls under the jurisdiction of the Sadashivanagar and Sanjaynagar traffic police stations. The construction is expected to take 18 months. The corridor is part of the BDA’s Rs 2,215-crore project to ease congestion at the Hebbal junction. The larger project includes a six-lane, cut-and-cover short tunnel between Hebbal junction and the Veterinary College, followed by an elevated corridor leading to Mehkri Circle, where a rotary flyover is planned.
